summary: The F_q[T] analogue of Fortune's conjecture is made precise and its elementary reduction is proved: with P_d the product of all monic irreducibles of degree <= d (n_d := deg P_d = sum_{e<=d} e*pi_q(e), so n_d ~ q^d) any nonconstant m of minimal degree with P_d + m irreducible is itself irreducible (up to a unit) whenever that minimal degree is <= 2d+1, since a reducible coprime offset has degree >= 2d+2. The exact statements of Keating-Rudnick (1204.0708), Bank-Bary-Soroker-Rosenzweig (1302.0625), Sawin (1809.05137), Sawin-Shusterman (1808.04001) and Ha (1601.06867) were verified verbatim from the papers; every one of them fails the crucial coupling n ~ q^d by an explicit margin (Lang-Weil constants and sqrt(q)-only savings for BBR; an explicit (n+2)^{2n-h} Betti factor for Sawin; squarefree averaged moduli and level 1/2+1/126 for Sawin-Shusterman; n/4 prescribed coefficients for Ha; q->infinity limits for KR/Hochfilzer). The only technology whose error is polynomial in the centre degree is the Weil Riemann Hypothesis itself, which yields a provable-sketch theorem: unconditionally, for every q and all large d, the Fortunate element F(q,d) exists and either is irreducible or has degree in [2d+2, n/2 + 2 log_q n + O(1)] — a statement strictly stronger than anything provable over Z (where the upper bound needs RH), and the honest "first Fortune-type theorem" available now. I also prove a clean micro-lemma: for q = p prime, no degree-1 offset ever makes T^p - T + m irreducible (bijectivity of the affine additive map), the same solvable-monodromy mechanism as BBR's short-interval counterexamples. The sharpest open target is d = 1: for every prime p >= 3 there is m with deg m in {2,3} and T^p - T + m irreducible, which with the proved pieces gives full FF-Fortune for d = 1; the identified attack is a polynomial-in-p bound on the Betti sum of Sawin's low-dimensional interval variety at the additive centre T^p - T — genuinely new mathematics, not a restatement of the archive's closed kernel, but with no existing mechanism (difficulty: high). Exact-arithmetic diagnostics in 18 cases (p up to 19, n up to 145) all confirm the conjecture, with observed Fortunate degree ~ log_q n, a square margin below the bound 2 log_q n exactly mirroring the integer picture. The q-fixed, d->infinity regime is flagged as isomorphic to the integer critical-length wall (stop-rule: not a route), while the d=1 large-p regime is new territory.
writeup:
# Function-field frontier for Fortune's conjecture: assessment

All labels follow the programme's epistemic rules: **proved** / **provable-sketch** / **gap** / **unverified** / **false**. Literature statements below were read verbatim from the cited arXiv texts via alphaXiv unless marked UNVERIFIED.

## 1. The precise analogue and the elementary reduction (proved)

**Setup.** Fix a prime power q. Let pi_q(e) denote the number of monic irreducibles of degree e in F_q[T], and

  P_d = prod_{deg pi <= d, pi monic irreducible} pi,  n_d := deg P_d = sum_{e<=d} e*pi_q(e).

Since sum_{e<=d} e*pi_q(e) = sum_{e<=d} sum_{c|e} mu(e/c) q^c, one gets n_1 = q, n_2 = q^2, n_3 = q^3+q^2-q, and in general q^d <= n_d = q^d(1 + q^{-1} + O(d q^{-2})); so **n_d ~ q^d** (verified numerically in code for all cases run, e.g. n = 105 for (q,d)=(3,4), n = 106 for (2,6)).

**Fortunate element.** Order nonzero polynomials by degree first, then by any fixed order on coefficient tuples (lex after ordering F_q). Define

  D(q,d) = min{ deg m : m in F_q[T] nonconstant, P_d + m irreducible },

and call any minimizing m a Fortunate element F(q,d). Discussion of the ordering: (i) constants are the units of F_q[T], so "m nonconstant" is the exact analogue of "m > 1" over Z (P_n + 1 = Euclid case excluded there; P_d + c here — and indeed T^p - T + c IS irreducible for c in F_p^*, the Artin–Schreier analogue of Euclid primes, correctly excluded). (ii) The tie-break within a degree is arbitrary and immaterial: the right, ordering-robust conjecture is that **every** minimal-degree m is irreducible (times a unit; exactly irreducible if one restricts to monic m — both conventions work identically below). (iii) Existence of F(q,d) is trivial (there are ~ q^n/n irreducibles of degree n = n_d, at most q of which equal P_d + constant).

**Lemma 1 (factor-degree floor). [proved]** Let 1 <= deg m < n_d and P_d + m irreducible. Then every irreducible factor of m has degree >= d+1. *Proof.* If pi | m with deg pi <= d then pi | P_d, so pi | P_d + m; since P_d + m is irreducible of degree n_d > deg pi, this forces P_d + m = (unit)·pi, impossible by degrees. ∎

**Theorem 2 (reduction). [proved]** Assume 2d+1 < n_d (true for all (q,d) except the degenerate (q,d) = (2,1), (2,2), (3,1); in the last, replace 2d+1 by n_d - 1 = 2 and the statement below still holds, vacuously stronger). If D(q,d) <= 2d+1, then every Fortunate element F(q,d) is a unit times an irreducible. *Proof.* deg F <= 2d+1 < n_d, so P_d + F is monic of degree n_d and Lemma 1 applies: all irreducible factors of F have degree >= d+1. If F were reducible (>= 2 irreducible factors with multiplicity), deg F >= 2(d+1) = 2d+2 > 2d+1, contradiction. ∎

**Dictionary check.** Over Z: composite F_n >= p_{n+1}^2, interval (P_n, P_n + p_{n+1}^2) of length ~ (log P_n)^2. Here: the "next primes" have degree d+1, "p_{n+1}^2" becomes degree 2(d+1) = 2d+2, and the Fortune-forcing family is {P_d + m : 1 <= deg m <= 2d+1}, of size q^{2d+2} - q ~ (q·n_d)^2, i.e. exponent h* := 2d+2 ~ 2 log_q n_d + 2. With deg ↔ log the analogy is exact: an interval of "(log of the centre)^2" size around a centre of size q^{n_d}. Expected number of irreducibles in the family ~ q^{2d+2}/n_d ~ q^{d+2}: heuristically overwhelming, exactly as over Z.

**Lemma 3 (degree-1 impossibility at d = 1, prime fields). [proved]** Let q = p >= 3 be prime. There is NO m of degree 1 with P_1 + m = T^p - T + m irreducible. *Proof.* Write m = aT + b, a != 0; then T^p - T + m = T^p - cT + b with c = 1 - a != 1. If c = 0: T^p + b = (T + b)^p (Frobenius), reducible. If c != 0,1: the F_p-linear map x -> x^p - cx on F_p has kernel {x : x^{p-1} = c} = {0} (since x^{p-1} = 1 for all x != 0 and c != 1), hence is a bijection of F_p; so x^p - cx = -b has a root in F_p and the polynomial has a linear factor; its degree p >= 3 makes it reducible. ∎ (Numerically confirmed: in all runs with d = 1, p in {3,...,19}, the scan exhausted all p(p-1) degree-1 candidates without success.)

Lemma 3 is the same mechanism as the **verified** anomalies of Bank–Bary-Soroker–Rosenzweig [arXiv:1302.0625, Prop. 6.1–6.3]: intervals around additive centres (t^{p^2}, t^{p^2+1}) contain NO irreducibles for eps < 2/k because the monodromy group is affine/projective-linear and has no long cycles. Around P_1 = T^q - T (itself additive) the degree-<=1 family is trapped in the affine group; degree >= 2 escapes it (numerics: successes always appear at degree 2). This is a structural caution AND a sharpening: the d=1 conjecture is exactly the assertion that the degree-2 perturbation family generates long cycles.

## 2. Survey of what is actually proved (exact statements, all verified from the papers)

**(a) Keating–Rudnick, arXiv:1204.0708** (Int. Math. Res. Not. 2014). Interval I(A;h) = A + P_{<=h}, |I| = q^{h+1}; nu(A;h) = sum of Lambda over I, f(0) != 0. **Theorem 2.1:** for h <= n-4 (stated h < n-3), lim_{q->infty} Var(nu)/q^{h+1} = n - h - 2, **n fixed, q -> infinity**. The mechanism (Theorem 4.1): Var = q^{h+1}( mean over primitive even chi mod T^{n-h} of |tr Theta_chi^n|^2 + O((n-h)/q^{n/2} + n^2/q) ), implied constant depending only on n; the input is Katz equidistribution of Frobenii in PU(n-h-2), again q -> infinity at fixed n-h. Also verified there: the interval-to-progression involution f*(T) = T^{deg f} f(1/T) with nu(T^{h+1}B; h) = Psi~(n; T^{n-h}, B*) (Lemma 4.2), and the Weil bound |Psi(n,chi)| <= (deg Q - 1) q^{n/2} for chi != chi_0 (eq. 3.33). **Regime: q -> infinity, n fixed; averaged over ALL centres.** No fixed-q content.

**(b) Bank–Bary-Soroker–Rosenzweig, arXiv:1302.0625** (Duke Math. J. 164 (2015)). **Theorem 2.3:** for any partition lambda of k = deg f, any prime power q, interval I = f + P_{<=m} with 3 <= m < k (m = 1 allowed if p ∤ k(k-1); m = 2 if p != 2 or deg f' > 1): |pi_q(I; lambda) - P(lambda) q^{m+1}| <= c(k) q^{m+1/2}, with c(k) depending only on k, produced by Lang–Weil applied to a variety built from the S_k-Galois closure — **c(k) unspecified and (from the construction) at least exponential in k**. Nontrivial only when q^{1/2} >> k·c(k): **q large compared to the degree of the centre**.

**(c) Sawin, arXiv:1809.05137** ("Square-root cancellation for sums of factorization functions over short intervals in function fields"). **Theorem 1.2 / Corollary 4.7:** for f monic of degree n, interval of size q^h (equivalently m = n-h prescribed top coefficients), |sum_{deg g < h} Lambda(f+g) - (interval size)| <= 6 (n+2)^{2n-h} q^{(1/2)(h + floor(n/p) - floor((n-h)/p) + 1)}. (The displayed main term "q^n" in the paper's Theorem 1.2/Cor. 4.7 is an evident typo for the interval size q^{n-m}; the underlying Proposition 4.2 has main term q^{n-m} dim(pi^{S_n}).) **The error constant is fully explicit and polynomial in nothing: (n+2)^{2n-h} is exponential in n.** The paper's own statement of the asymptotic regime: n -> infinity with h/n >= (1/p + 2 log_q(n+2)) / ((p-1)/p + 2 log_q(n+2)) - eps; and the abstract states the results "are not yet nontrivial in the large n limit" (fixed q). Effectively the theorem needs q >= n^{4n/h + o(1)}, i.e. q at least polynomially large in n even for h comparable to n.

**(d) Sawin–Shusterman, arXiv:1808.04001** ("On the Chowla and twin primes conjectures over F_q[T]", Ann. of Math. 196 (2022) — venue UNVERIFIED, statements verified from arXiv v2). **Theorem 1.1 (twin primes):** for odd p and q > 685090 p^2: #{f : |f| = X, f and f+h prime} ~ S_q(h) X / log_q^2 X as X -> infinity through powers of q, with power saving; **fixed q, degree -> infinity, but averaged over the centre f** — it says nothing about one prescribed centre. **Theorem 1.3 (Chowla):** k-point, q > p^2 k^2 e^2. **Theorem 1.7:** Möbius level of distribution 1 - eta for q > p^2 e^2 (2/eta - 1)^2. **Theorem 1.9 (Lambda level of distribution):** for delta < 1/126 and q > p^2 e^2 ((51-26delta)/(1-126delta))^2, for **squarefree** M with X^{1/2+delta} >= |M|: sum_{f = a mod M} Lambda(f) = X/phi(M) + o(X/|M|). **Theorem 2.1 (character sums):** for **squarefree** modulus g of degree m and t <= m: |sum_{deg h < t} chi(f+h)| <= (q^{1/2}+1) binom(m-1, t) q^{t/2} — nontrivial for intervals of length a small constant fraction of the conductor degree once q > (e·m/t)^{2+o(1)}: this is the beyond-Burgess engine, **requires squarefree modulus**. **Theorem 1.11:** Möbius sign changes in intervals |f|^{3/7} for q a power of 3 — below the 1/2 barrier, but for mu, not Lambda. **Theorem 1.12:** sum_{|f| <= X, f = 1 mod P^k} mu(f) = o(X/|P|^k) whenever X/|P|^k -> infinity, q a power of 3 — cancellation in a SINGLE residue class to a prime-power modulus of arbitrary relative size, the structurally closest fixed-q theorem to what Fortune needs; but (i) mu, not Lambda (parity), (ii) class 1 only, (iii) the paper itself notes Maier obstructions for general classes.

**(e) Ha, arXiv:1601.06867** (Finite Fields Appl. 40 (2016) — journal UNVERIFIED, statements verified from arXiv). **Theorem 1.1/1.3 (circle method, fixed q!):** an irreducible of degree n exists with r coefficients prescribed **in arbitrary positions** for r <= n/4 - log_q n - 1 (q >= 16), r <= n/5 (q >= 5, n >= 97), r <= n/10 (all q, n >= 52); error O(q^{3n/4}) plus a q^{-C_2/rho}-type saving. State of the art for prescribed coefficients at fixed q: **a quarter of the coefficients — Fortune needs all but ~2 log_q n of them.**

**(f) Fixed-q variance.** Sawin–Shusterman list "variance of Möbius in short intervals" as future work (§1.5, 2019). Hochfilzer, arXiv:2102.06415, generalizes KR's short-interval variance to Galois-twisted von Mangoldt functions via Sawin's equidistribution (arXiv:1805.04330) — but again **q = q_0^k -> infinity at fixed characteristic** (Theorem 9.4: lim_{q->infty} Var/q^{nw+h+1} = min{n, s_Q(rho)}, h <= n-5). I found no fixed-q variance theorem for Lambda in short intervals; its existence in later literature is UNVERIFIED-negative (searched, none surfaced).

## 3. The crux: the coupling n_d ~ q^d (proved arithmetic on verified statements)

The Fortune-forcing exponent is h* = 2d+2, main term q^{h*}/n_d ~ q^{d+2}. Test each verified technology against (n, h, q) = (n_d, 2d+2, q), n_d ~ q^d:

- **Weil RH (explicit formula + involution; ingredients all displayed in KR):** error per residue class <= (n-h-1) q^{n/2} — the ONLY error in the entire surveyed corpus that is **polynomial in the centre degree n with absolute constants**. It survives the coupling, but only down to h ~ n/2: need q^{h+1} > (n-h) q^{n/2} + 3n q^{n/2}, i.e. h >= n/2 + 2 log_q n + O(1). Result: Target Theorem 1 below. It cannot go lower: this IS the RH barrier.
- **BBR:** even granting c(k) = 1, error/main = c q^{m+1/2} · n / q^{m+1} = n q^{-1/2} ~ q^{d - 1/2} >= q^{1/2}: **fails for every d >= 1**; the failure is structural (Lang–Weil saves exactly sqrt(q) regardless of interval size, while the main term is thinned by 1/n ~ q^{-d}).
- **Sawin:** error/main >= (n+2)^{2n-h} q^{-(h/2 + O(1))}; with h = 2d+2, n ~ q^d this is exp(2 q^d · d log q - O(d log q)): fails by a factor exponential in n. Even at h = n-1 it fails at fixed q (needs q > n^{2+o(1)}). The explicit bottleneck is the Betti-sum bound B(pi) <= 3(n+2)^{n+m} (Katz's general bound for complete intersections) — see the attack plan.
- **Sawin–Shusterman:** after the involution, {P_d + m : deg m <= h} is the single residue class (P_d)* mod T^{n-h}: modulus a **perfect power of T** (excluded from Thms 1.7/1.9/2.1 which need squarefree moduli), a **single class** (excluded from all averaged level-of-distribution statements), and conductor exponent (n-h)/n = 1 - O((log n)/n) (their level for Lambda tops out at 1/2 + 1/126). Their Thm 1.12 (mu, class 1 mod P^k, q = 3^nu) shows the modulus shape itself is not fatal for parity-free statements — but converting mu-cancellation to prime detection in a single class reinstates the full parity/convolution machinery and dies.
- **Ha:** needs n - h ~ n - 2 log_q n prescribed coefficients vs. his n/4 ceiling: fails by a factor ~4 in the exponent — and his method (circle method + Weil on major arcs) again cannot pass sqrt-of-conductor for the minor arcs.
- **KR / Hochfilzer variance:** q -> infinity limits with n-dependent constants (Katz/Sawin equidistribution): the coupling is outside their hypotheses; moreover variance over all q^{n-h-1} intervals cannot isolate the one interval at P_d (P_d's affine-symmetry orbit has size only ~ q^3).

**Conclusion (task 3).** Under the coupling, the only surviving error shape is (poly in n)·q^{n/2}, i.e. the Riemann Hypothesis itself, and the sharpest provable partial statement is the half-degree theorem below. No known result gives irreducibles in the Fortune-forcing range h = 2d+2 in ANY regime: the fixed-q regime reproduces the integer critical-length wall exactly (individual class, conductor exponent -> 1, parity), and the large-q regime is killed by thin-class counting (the target class "n-cycle" has density 1/n ~ q^{-d}, below every sqrt(q)-type equidistribution error).

## 4. Numerical diagnostics (proved computations; diagnostics only, not evidence of the asymptotic)

Exact arithmetic over F_p (own implementation: early-abort distinct-degree irreducibility test; script `ff_fortune.py` in the session scratchpad). For each case: minimal m in (degree, lex) order with P_d + m irreducible; check deg m <= 2d+1 and m irreducible.

| p | d | n = deg P_d | deg F | bound 2d+1 | F irreducible |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3..19 (7 primes) | 1 | p | 2 | 3 (2 for p=3) | yes, all |
| 2 | 3/4/5/6 | 10/22/52/106 | 4/5/7/7 | 7/9/11/13 | yes, all |
| 3 | 2/3/4 | 9/33/105 | 3/4/6 | 5/7/9 | yes, all |
| 5 | 2/3 | 25/145 | 3/4 | 5/7 | yes, all |
| 7 | 2 | 49 | 3 | 5 | yes |
| 11 | 2 | 121 | 3 | 5 | yes |

18/18 conform. Observed deg F ~ log_q n + O(1) (e.g. (2,6): 7 vs log_2 106 = 6.7), a full square below the allowed q^{2d+2} ~ (q n)^2 — the same margin structure as over Z (F_n ~ c log P_n vs allowed (log P_n)^2). Degree-1 always fails at d = 1 (Lemma 3 confirmed). Prime-power q untested (implementation is prime-field only).

## 5. Target statements and attack plan (task 4)

**Conjecture FF-Fortune.** For every prime power q and d >= 1 (with 2d+1 < n_d): D(q,d) <= 2d+1; equivalently (Theorem 2) every Fortunate element of P_d is irreducible up to units.

**Target Theorem 1 (write-up ready). [provable-sketch — complete proof assembled from verified ingredients, not independently refereed]** There is an absolute constant n_0 such that for all q and d with n = n_d >= n_0, and h = ceil(n/2) + ceil(2 log_q n) + 2:
D(q,d) <= h. Hence unconditionally: **either F(q,d) is irreducible (up to a unit), or 2d+2 <= deg F(q,d) <= n/2 + 2 log_q n + O(1).**
*Proof sketch.* Write P_d = T^{h+1}B + g_0, B monic of degree n-h-1, so {P_d + m : deg m <= h} = I(T^{h+1}B; h). By the involution (KR Lemma 4.2) and orthogonality over the q^{n-h-1} even characters mod T^{n-h} (KR eq. 4.22, verified): nu(T^{h+1}B; h) = q^{h+1}(1 - q^{-n}) + q^{-(n-h-1)} sum_{chi != chi_0 even} chi(B*) Psi(n, chi), and |Psi(n,chi)| <= (n-h-1) q^{n/2} by Weil (KR eq. 3.33). So nu >= q^{h+1}(1-q^{-n}) - (n-h-1) q^{n/2}. The Lambda-mass of proper prime powers of degree n is <= 2n q^{n/2}. For the stated h the difference exceeds q (the number of constant offsets), so some nonconstant m with deg m <= h gives P_d + m irreducible. ∎
Significance, honestly stated: over Z the analogous upper bound deg-analogue F_n << (log P_n)·P_n^{1/2}-type statement needs RH; here it is unconditional because Weil's RH is a theorem. It is a genuine "first Fortunate-degree theorem in any setting", but it is at the RH barrier, an exponential factor (q^{n/2} vs q^{2d+2}, i.e. sqrt(x) vs log^2 x) above the conjecture.

**Target Theorem 2 (the open crown; sharpest attackable full-Fortune case). [gap]** For every prime p >= 3 there exists m in F_p[T] with deg m in {2,3} such that T^p - T + m is irreducible. *Consequences (with proved Lemma 3 + Theorem 2): FF-Fortune holds for d = 1 over every prime field, and deg F(p,1) = 2 for all p where a quadratic works (all tested p).* This would be the first full Fortune-type theorem in any setting: an infinite family (all p), not a finite verification.

**Attack plan for Target 2, with honest difficulty assessment.**
1. *Geometric route (identified bottleneck).* The family {T^p - T + m : deg m <= 3} is exactly Sawin's interval variety X_{n,m,c} (n = p, codim m = p-4, dim = 4) at the additive centre c = coefficients of T^p - T. Sawin's Proposition 4.2 gives |sum_I Lambda - q^4| <= B(pi) q^{(1/2)(4 + floor(n/p) - floor((n-4)/p) + 1)} = B(pi) p^3, and the theorem follows from **B(pi) = o(p)** — versus Katz's general bound B <= 3(p+2)^{2p-4}. So the precise open problem is: *polynomial-in-p bounds for the compactly supported Betti sum of the 4-dimensional variety {a in A^p : elementary symmetric functions e_1..e_{p-4}(a) match T^p - T}*, exploiting the additive structure (T^p - T = prod_{alpha in F_p}(T - alpha); the variety contains the S_p-orbit of the F_p-point (0,1,...,p-1); the perturbation directions are the 4 lowest symmetric functions). Generic complete intersections of codimension p-4 have exponential Betti sums (Bezout), so the additive structure must do real work; whether it does is unknown. Difficulty: **high, wild-ramification / char-p geometry with no template**, but it is a concrete cohomology computation, finitely checkable per p, and — crucially for the stop-rule — **not a restatement of the programme's closed kernel** (no reciprocal frame, no critical-length character sums, no parity: the obstruction is a Betti-number bound, a different mathematics).
2. *Explicit-construction route.* Find a closed-form c(p) with T^p - T + T^2 - c irreducible (numerics: such c exists for every tested p, e.g. c = -1 mod 3, ... no pattern verified). Any Artin–Schreier-tower or Dickson-type identity giving one irreducible per p suffices. Difficulty: unknown; cheap to explore computationally (next diagnostic: factorization statistics of T^p - T + T^2 - c over all c in F_p for p up to a few hundred, testing whether #{c : irreducible} ~ p/p · p = O(p/p)-normalized S_p-statistics or shows exploitable bias).
3. *What will NOT work (stop-rule audit).* (i) Regime q fixed, d -> infinity: after the involution this is prime detection in ONE residue class to the modulus T^{n-h} with conductor exponent 1 - O((log n)/n) — the same individual-class/parity wall at the critical length that the archive has closed over Z; the free FF RH only buys exponent 1/2, exactly as over Z; proposals here must be rejected unless they overcome individual-class detection beyond conductor^{1/2 + 1/126}, which nothing surveyed does. The one FF-specific glimmer — the p-th-power/derivative mechanism that gives Möbius results below the 1/2 barrier (SS Thms 1.11, 1.12, verified) — is parity-blocked from Lambda by the same convolution obstruction as over Z. (ii) Any generic large-q equidistribution (BBR-type) for d >= 1: killed by thin-class arithmetic (main term q^{-d}-thin vs sqrt(q)-error), proved above.

**Secondary targets (ranked).** (T3) Fixed-q variance of Lambda in short intervals (open per the surveyed record; SS's own future-work list) — would be the FF analogue of the programme's Theorem 2.4 input (12.2), but note it would give Fortune-type conclusions only for almost-all centres at the corresponding h, and only for h where the variance is provable; still the natural "Paper III over F_q[T]". (T4) Extend Target Theorem 1 below n/2 for the specific centre P_d using its affine symmetry P_d(aT+b) = c·P_d(T) — expected gain at most a bounded factor; low value. (T5) FF-Fortune for d = 1 over F_{p^2} etc. (Artin–Schreier analysis of degree-1 offsets differs there: for q = p^nu, T^p - cT - b CAN be irreducible... but note deg P_1 = q not p for q non-prime, so the d=1 family is T^q - T + m; untested, and the Lemma 3 analysis does not directly transfer — left open).

## 6. Bottom line

The function-field analogue is exact, the reduction is airtight, and the setting delivers one real, immediately writable theorem (Target Theorem 1: unconditional Fortunate-degree bound at the RH scale — impossible over Z) plus one sharply posed open problem (Target Theorem 2, d = 1) whose obstruction is genuinely different mathematics (Betti sums of low-dimensional interval varieties in char p) rather than the archive's closed kernel. The full conjecture at fixed q with d -> infinity is the integer problem in disguise and should not be advertised as a route. The realistic value of this frontier to the programme: a citable first theorem, a clean testbed (every (q,d) finitely checkable; 18/18 diagnostics conform), and a precise localization of where "new mathematics" would have to live on the algebraic side (B(pi) = o(p) for the additive-centre interval variety), complementing the analytic localization (sparse exceptional-set bound) already recorded in the addendum.

key_claims.claim: FF reduction: if the minimal nonconstant m with P_d + m irreducible has degree <= 2d+1 (and 2d+1 < deg P_d), then every such minimal m is irreducible up to a unit; a reducible offset coprime to P_d has degree >= 2d+2.
key_claims.notes: Full proof in writeup (Lemma 1 + Theorem 2), including the degenerate exceptions (q,d) = (2,1),(2,2),(3,1). Exact analogue of composite F_n >= p_{n+1}^2.

key_claims.claim: deg P_d = sum_{e<=d} e*pi_q(e) = q^d (1 + q^{-1} + O(d q^{-2})), so the centre degree is coupled to q as n ~ q^d and the Fortune-forcing interval exponent is 2d+2 ~ 2 log_q n.
key_claims.notes: Elementary from the prime polynomial theorem; cross-checked numerically (n = 105 at (3,4), 106 at (2,6), 145 at (5,3)).

key_claims.claim: For q = p prime, p >= 3, no degree-1 offset m makes T^p - T + m irreducible (affine additive map is bijective or the polynomial is a p-th power).
key_claims.notes: Short complete proof in writeup; numerically confirmed for p = 3..19. Same solvable-monodromy mechanism as BBR's verified short-interval counterexamples (their Props 6.1-6.2).

key_claims.claim: Exact statements and regimes of Keating-Rudnick 1204.0708 (variance, q->infty, n fixed, h <= n-4), BBR 1302.0625 (short intervals, error c(k) q^{m+1/2} with Lang-Weil constant c(k) depending only on k, m >= 3), Sawin 1809.05137 (explicit error 6(n+2)^{2n-h} q^{(1/2)(h+floor(n/p)-floor((n-h)/p)+1)}, not nontrivial at fixed q large n), Sawin-Shusterman 1808.04001 (twin primes q > 685090 p^2 odd averaged over centres; Lambda level of distribution 1/2+1/126 for squarefree moduli; Mobius class-1 mod P^k cancellation for q = 3^nu; char sums (q^{1/2}+1) binom(m-1,t) q^{t/2} for squarefree moduli), Ha 1601.06867 (fixed q, up to n/4 - log_q n - 1 prescribed coefficients, arbitrary positions).
key_claims.notes: All read verbatim from the arXiv texts via alphaXiv in this session. One evident typo noted in Sawin Thm 1.2/Cor 4.7 (main term printed q^n, must be the interval size, per his Prop 4.2). Journal attributions (Annals for SS, FFA for Ha) UNVERIFIED.

key_claims.claim: No surveyed result reaches the Fortune-forcing range h = 2d+2 under the coupling n ~ q^d, in any regime: BBR fails for every d >= 1 even with c(k) = 1 (needs d < 1/2); Sawin fails by an exp(2 q^d d log q) factor; SS is blocked by squarefree/averaged moduli and level <= 1/2 + 1/126 vs needed 1 - o(1); Ha by n/4 vs n - O(log n) prescribed coefficients; KR/Hochfilzer by the q->infty limit.
key_claims.notes: Arithmetic on the verified statements, shown in writeup Section 3. Scope limitation: 'no technology exists anywhere in the literature' is not claimed; the surveyed corpus is the papers listed plus targeted searches that surfaced nothing stronger.

key_claims.claim: Target Theorem 1: unconditionally, for all q and all d with n = deg P_d large, there is a nonconstant m with deg m <= n/2 + 2 log_q n + O(1) and P_d + m irreducible; hence F(q,d) is irreducible or has degree in [2d+2, n/2 + 2 log_q n + O(1)]. This is the sharpest provable Fortune-type statement and is stronger than anything provable over Z (where the analogue needs RH).
key_claims.notes: Complete proof assembled in writeup from independently verified ingredients (KR's involution Lemma 4.2, eq. 4.22 orthogonality identity, Weil bound eq. 3.33, prime-power mass bound). Not refereed; bookkeeping of the O(1) not optimized. The claim that the Z-analogue requires RH is standard but UNVERIFIED against a specific reference here.

key_claims.claim: The polynomial-in-centre-degree error property singled out in task 3 is possessed ONLY by the Weil explicit-formula bound (error (n-h) q^{n/2}, absolute constants) among all surveyed technologies; it survives the coupling exactly down to h ~ n/2 and no further.
key_claims.notes: Follows from the verified error shapes; this is the precise sense in which FF gives 'RH for free' but nothing below it for individual intervals.

key_claims.claim: Fixed-q variance of Lambda (or Mobius) in short intervals over F_q[t] is open as of the verified record: Sawin-Shusterman list it as future work (2019); Hochfilzer 2102.06415 and its input (Sawin 1805.04330) are q -> infinity at fixed characteristic.
key_claims.notes: Negative claim: targeted alphaXiv searches surfaced no fixed-q variance theorem, but absence of evidence in two searches is not proof of absence in the 2021-2026 literature.

key_claims.claim: Diagnostics: in all 18 computed cases (p in {2,...,19}, deg P_d up to 145) the Fortunate element exists with degree <= 2d+1 and is irreducible; observed deg F ~ log_q n + O(1), a full square below the allowed bound, mirroring the integer margin.
key_claims.notes: Exact-arithmetic computation (script in scratchpad, own DDF-based irreducibility test); diagnostic only per programme rules, no asymptotic inference. Prime-power q untested.

key_claims.claim: Target Theorem 2 (open): for every prime p >= 3 some m with deg m in {2,3} makes T^p - T + m irreducible; with the proved pieces this yields full FF-Fortune for d = 1 over all prime fields, the identified 'first full Fortune-type theorem' candidate. The precise bottleneck of the geometric attack is a polynomial-in-p bound on the Betti sum B(pi) of Sawin's 4-dimensional interval variety at the additive centre T^p - T (versus Katz's exponential general bound 3(p+2)^{2p-4}); B(pi) = o(p) suffices.
key_claims.notes: The sufficiency of B(pi) = o(p) follows from Sawin's verified Prop 4.2 with (n, m, q) = (p, p-4, p). No mechanism for the Betti bound is known; generic complete intersections of this codimension have exponential Betti sums, so the additive structure must be exploited. Passes the archive stop-rule: not a restatement of the closed reciprocal-frame kernel.

key_claims.claim: The regime q fixed, d -> infinity is isomorphic to the integer critical-length wall (single residue class mod T^{n-h}, conductor exponent 1 - o(1), parity) and must not be advertised as a route; FF-specific parity-free tools (SS derivative trick, Mobius below the 1/2 barrier) do not transfer to Lambda in a single class.
key_claims.notes: Stop-rule audit: the involution identification is exact (KR Lemma 4.2); the SS mechanisms verified to require squarefree moduli or to concern Mobius only. 'Must not transfer by any future method' is of course not claimed - the flag is that current mechanisms provably do not.
